clue.text: Old spinster with craft but lacking a teasing quality

indicators.note: lacking says the following letter is missing from the spinster's name

parts.note: Arachne, the weaver of Greek myth turned into a spider, is an ancient spinner of thread
SS, steamship, is a craft at sea

explanation.surface: An elderly unmarried woman with a boat turns out to have no playful charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinster' looks like an unmarried woman but here is one who spins: Arachne. 'Lacking a' removes one A from ARACHNE to leave ARCHNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being arch means being playfully mischievous, so the abstract noun names a roguish, teasing manner.

clue.text: Unfortunately, a chap is unable To communicate

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sadly, a man finds he cannot express himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone with a brain disorder that destroys speech or language understanding.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' as a pawnbroker is old British slang; 'broker' looks like a dealer in general.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a red garnet cut with a rounded top, a precious stone.

clue.text: Score for T.U.C.

clue.text: Most sympathetic, moreover, on feminine questions

explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the pieces one after another, as in a down entry.

clue.text: Part-time barman, insisting on a drink

explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'insisting on': insiSTING On.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is an old name for strong ale or beer, a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Conjecture, appropriate to support specious conclusion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like the adjective 'fitting' but is the verb, to take for oneself.

clue.text: Spirit in America, young at heart

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Sleeve in man's coat, for example

clue.text: Formerly fee, or other settlement

clue.text: English resort with sort of bath that's a financial disaster

explanation.walkthrough: The South Sea Bubble was the 1720 collapse of the South Sea Company's shares, ruining many British investors.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1720 share crash is history's famous example of a speculative bubble bursting and wiping out investors.

clue.text: "Can this ____ hold the vasty fields of France?" (Hen.V)

definitions.text: "Can this ____ hold the vasty fields of France?" (Hen.V)

parts.words: "Can this ____ hold the vasty fields of France?" (Hen.V)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from the Chorus's prologue to Shakespeare's Henry V, where the theatre is called a small arena for fighting birds

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's Henry V asking whether a small stage can contain France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chorus apologises that the playhouse, a small ring like one for cock-fighting, must stand in for the battlefields of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit where gamecocks were set to fight became a figure for any small arena, here Shakespeare's theatre.

clue.text: Squire's first to go after wild beasts using hounds

explanation.definitionFit: Bassets are short-legged scent dogs, a breed of hunting dog.

clue.text: Forecast moving date is met
